MATCHUPS.INTRO2: Strategies and tips for your clashes!

WAVEMANAGEMENT.SUBTITLE0: Control your minion wave to take over your lane!
WAVEMANAGEMENT.CONTENT1:
Wave management means controlling where and when your minion wave meets the enemy one. Depending on where the minions fight, you gain safety, gold, experience, or time to act elsewhere on the map.
It is one of the most important skills in the game: it matters in every lane, and even for the jungler, who picks their ganks based on where the waves are.

CONTENT2.INTRO1: There are 3 types of minion waves:
CONTENT2.LIST1: <bold>Standard wave:</bold> 3 melee minions and 3 caster minions.
CONTENT2.LIST2: <bold>Cannon wave:</bold> a standard wave + a cannon minion (also called siege minion), which is tougher and worth more gold.
CONTENT2.LIST3: <bold>Super wave:</bold> a standard wave + a very tough super minion. It only spawns in a lane whose inhibitor is destroyed.
CONTENT2.INTRO2:
The first wave spawns at 0:30, then a new wave leaves each base every 30 seconds. The pace then speeds up: one wave every 25 seconds from 14:00, then every 20 seconds from 30:00.
Cannon waves follow this cycle:
CONTENT2.LIST5: <bold>Before 14:00:</bold> Standard wave -> Standard wave -> Cannon wave.
CONTENT2.LIST7: <bold>After 25:00:</bold> every wave has a cannon minion.
CONTENT2.LIST8: <bold>Inhibitor destroyed:</bold> in that lane, the cannon minion is replaced by a super minion every wave, until the inhibitor respawns (5 minutes). If all 3 inhibitors of a team are destroyed, every lane gets 2 super minions per wave.
CONTENT2.INTRO3: <italic>Bonus info:</italic> from 3:30, the team with the higher average level gives its minions an edge: they deal more damage to enemy minions and take less from them. The bonus grows with the level gap and with the number of towers destroyed in that lane. It only applies to minion-versus-minion fights, not to champions.

WAVEMANAGEMENT.TITLE4: When to go back to base

CONTENT4.INTRO: A good <term k="BACK">back</term> (recall to base) makes you lose as few minions as possible and brings you back to lane with a real power gain.
CONTENT4.LIST1: <bold>Based on your gold:</bold> go back when you can buy an important component or a full item. Going back for a small purchase costs you one or two waves for almost nothing.
CONTENT4.LIST2: <bold>After a kill, or when your opponent goes back:</bold> push your wave into their tower first, then recall. You come back with your items while they lose minions under their tower.
CONTENT4.LIST3: <bold>On a cannon wave:</bold> this wave has more minions and the cannon minion is worth more gold. Pushed into the enemy tower, it takes longer to be destroyed, which gives you time to go back and return while losing little.
CONTENT4.LIST4: <bold>Avoid recalling in front of a big enemy wave:</bold> if a big enemy wave reaches your tower while you are away, the tower kills part of it (gold and experience lost for you), and your opponent can then hold the wave in front of your tower when you return.
CONTENT4.LIST5: <bold>No time to push?</bold> Prepare your recall a few waves ahead with a <term k="SLOW_PUSH">slow push</term>: the big wave crashes into the enemy tower as you go back, and your opponent has to stay and farm it.
CONTENT4.LIST6: <bold>Think about objectives:</bold> go back early enough to be back, with your items, before a dragon or another objective spawns. Recalling right before it spawns leaves your team outnumbered.

WAVEMANAGEMENT.CONTENT5:
Freezing means keeping the wave still close to your tower, but outside its range. You only kill minions with the last hit: your opponent then has to walk far from their tower to farm, and becomes exposed to your jungler.

For a freeze to hold, the enemy wave must have slightly more minions than yours. It pushes a little toward you, but since your reinforcements arrive sooner (your base is closer), both sides balance out and the wave stays in place.

CONTENT6.LIST1: Only last-hit enemy minions: every extra bit of damage moves your wave forward and breaks the freeze.
CONTENT6.LIST2: Always keep a few more enemy minions than yours. The closer the wave is to your tower, the more you need (see the picture below).
CONTENT6.LIST3: If your minions are dead and the enemy wave walks toward your tower, stand in front of it: with no other target, the minions attack you and stop instead of entering the tower’s range. This is called “tanking the wave”.
CONTENT6.LIST4: If the enemy wave gets too big to tank safely, kill just enough minions to get back to the right gap, without pushing it.
CONTENT6.LIST5:
The closer the wave is to your tower, the sooner your next minions arrive: you therefore need to leave more enemy minions alive to keep the freeze.
The picture shows how many extra enemy minions you need depending on where the wave is.

CONTENT7.LIST1: <bold>The enemy jungler is a threat:</bold> freeze near your tower to farm safely; your opponent is the one who has to walk up.
CONTENT7.LIST2: <bold>You are behind:</bold> after a death or a tough lane, freezing lets you get gold and experience back without taking risks.
CONTENT7.LIST3: <bold>Your opponent recalls without pushing:</bold> keep the wave in front of your tower; when they come back, they will have to walk up to farm.
CONTENT7.LIST4: <bold>You are ahead:</bold> stand between your opponent and their wave. If they cannot walk up without risking death, they lose minions, and therefore gold and experience, every wave.

WAVEMANAGEMENT.CONTENT8:
Denies minions to your opponent if they cannot walk up.
Exposes them to your jungler if they walk up to farm.
You farm near your tower, safe from ganks.
Great to catch up on gold and experience.

You are stuck in your lane: your opponent can use that time to help elsewhere (roam).
Hard to hold against a champion who clears waves very fast.
The wave keeps growing: sooner or later you will have to kill it or let it move.
WAVEMANAGEMENT.CONTENT9:
Slow pushing means moving the wave forward slowly, killing only part of the enemy minions. Your surviving minions join the next wave: your wave grows over the minutes, then crashes all at once into the enemy tower.

Your opponent then has to choose: stay under their tower to collect this huge wave (and stay put), or leave it to their tower and lose a lot of gold and experience.
WAVEMANAGEMENT.SUBTITLE10: How to slow push a lane?
WAVEMANAGEMENT.CONTENT10: Kill the enemy caster minions first (the most fragile ones) and only last-hit the others. Your wave keeps a numbers advantage and moves forward slowly, over two or three waves. If you kill everything too fast, you are fast pushing instead.
WAVEMANAGEMENT.SUBTITLE11: When to slow push a lane?

CONTENT11.LIST1: <bold>Before leaving your lane:</bold> for an objective or a roam, the big wave hits the enemy tower while you are away. Your opponent has to stay and farm it and cannot follow you.
CONTENT11.LIST2: <bold>Before going back to base:</bold> the wave crashes into the enemy tower while you are gone, so you lose almost nothing.
CONTENT11.LIST3: <bold>To set up a <term k="DIVE">dive</term>:</bold> a big wave absorbs the tower shots, which lets you and your jungler attack your opponent under their tower with less risk.

WAVEMANAGEMENT.CONTENT12:
Fast pushing means killing the enemy wave as fast as possible, so that your minions quickly reach the enemy tower and crash into it.

Your opponent then has two options: stay under their tower to collect their minions, which ties them to their lane, or give them up and lose gold and experience. And under their tower, farming is harder: the tower also hits the minions, so they have to adjust their attacks to land the last hit.

Meanwhile, you are free: go back to base without missing minions, help your jungler or an ally, or place vision.
WAVEMANAGEMENT.SUBTITLE13: How to fast push a lane?

CONTENT13.LIST1: Attack enemy minions nonstop, not only for the last hit.
CONTENT13.LIST2: Use your area abilities to hit the whole wave at once, then finish the remaining minions with your attacks.
CONTENT13.LIST3: The cannon minion is the toughest: if it is left alone, your minions stop to hit it. Finish it yourself so your wave keeps moving.

WAVEMANAGEMENT.SUBTITLE14: When to fast push a lane?

CONTENT14.LIST1: <bold>Your opponent is dead or in base:</bold> quickly send the wave into their tower. It will destroy part of the minions before they return: gold and experience lost for them.
CONTENT14.LIST2: <bold>Before going back to base:</bold> the wave crashes into the enemy tower, your opponent has to stay and farm it, and you recall without missing a wave.
CONTENT14.LIST3: <bold>Before leaving your lane:</bold> to join a fight, an objective or help an ally, push first. Busy farming under their tower, your opponent cannot follow you right away. This is called having <term k="PRIO">priority</term>.
CONTENT14.LIST4: <bold>Against a champion who farms poorly under tower:</bold> some champions struggle to land last hits under their tower. Forcing them to do it costs them minions.

WAVEMANAGEMENT.CONTENT15: <bold>Important:</bold> pushing your wave takes you away from your tower. Before a slow push or a fast push, check where the enemy jungler is (vision, last seen on the map) so you do not get caught.

CONTENT1B.LIST1: <bold>Numbers win:</bold> the wave with more minions (or more health) wins the fight against the other one, then moves toward the opposing tower.
CONTENT1B.LIST2: <bold>Survivors stack up:</bold> if a few of your minions survive, they join the next wave. Your wave grows from one wave to the next.
CONTENT1B.LIST3: <bold>After a crash, the wave comes back:</bold> once your wave is destroyed by the enemy tower (it <term k="CRASH">crashes</term>), the next clash happens closer to that tower, and the wave naturally drifts back toward you.
CONTENT1B.LIST4: <bold>You set the balance:</bold> by killing more or fewer enemy minions, you choose which way the wave moves. This is the basis of the three strategies in this guide: freezing, slow pushing and fast pushing.

LANING.SUBTITLE0: Dominate your opponent from the very first minutes!

CONTENT1.INTRO1: The laning phase is the first minutes of the game, when each player faces their direct opponent in their lane. The goal: collect more gold and experience than them, without dying. Each lane has its own specifics:
CONTENT1.LIST1: <bold>Top:</bold> the most isolated lane. Often long duels, and the Teleport summoner spell to get back to lane quickly or join a fight elsewhere.
CONTENT1.LIST2: <bold>Mid:</bold> the shortest lane, in the middle of the map. Pushing your wave quickly lets you go help your jungler or the other lanes.
CONTENT1.LIST3: <bold>Bot:</bold> a marksman (<term k="ADC">ADC</term>) and a support play two versus two. Trades are decided by four players, and dragons spawn right next to the lane.
CONTENT1.INTRO2: Playing your lane well is not only about winning your duel: the gold and experience you earn here make you stronger for the rest of the game.

LANING.CONTENT2:
The last hit is landing the killing blow on minions: only the champion who lands it gets the minion’s gold. Experience, however, is shared between nearby champions when the minion dies, even if they did not kill it.

It is the main source of gold early in the game. Missing minions adds up fast: a few badly farmed waves are worth the gold of a kill. To improve, watch the minions’ health bars, learn how much damage your basic attack deals, and practice in the Practice Tool.

Last hitting is also the basis of wave management: by choosing which minions to kill and when, you control where the wave is (see the Wave Management guide).
LANING.CONTENT3: A <term k="TRADE">trade</term> is an exchange of damage between you and your opponent, with basic attacks or abilities. A good trade is one where you deal more damage than you take.

CONTENT4.LIST1: <bold>Hit them while they farm:</bold> to kill a minion, your opponent has to walk up and attack; they become predictable and vulnerable. Watch the health of your minions and punish them as they come for their last hit.
CONTENT4.LIST2: <bold>Use their cooldowns:</bold> if your opponent uses an important ability to farm or attack you, engage while it is on <term k="COOLDOWN">cooldown</term>. Making your opponent waste a spell (<term k="BAIT">baiting</term>) is covered in the next chapter.
CONTENT4.LIST3: <bold>Watch the minions:</bold> when you attack an enemy champion near their minions, those minions target you. Early in the game their damage is significant: avoid long trades in the middle of a big enemy wave.
CONTENT4.LIST4: <bold>Harass from range:</bold> <term k="POKE">poking</term> means hitting your opponent with long-range attacks or abilities without committing. They then have to play carefully, miss minions or use their potions. Some champions are built for it (Ziggs or Xerath, for example, far more than Garen). Once your opponent is weakened, you can engage.
CONTENT4.LIST5: <bold>Manage the distance:</bold> <term k="SPACING">spacing</term> is staying at the right distance from your opponent: close enough to use your abilities, far enough to avoid theirs. If you outrange them (a ranged champion against a melee one, for example), hit them every time they walk up to a minion.

LANING.CONTENT51:
Tip: during a trade, step into a bush to break your opponent’s vision. As long as they cannot see you, they cannot target you with basic attacks or targeted spells: their abilities have to be cast blind.

This does not work if they already have vision in that bush (a ward placed in it, or an ally standing inside).
LANING.CONTENT5:
Trades are even better when you are a level ahead of your opponent, or right after a power spike (your ultimate at level 6, a finished item…). Good wave management also helps you trade without losing minions.

Pick your moment: an opponent near their tower at full health is hard to threaten. And if you start a trade right before an enemy gank, your spells will be on cooldown at the worst time.

Every matchup calls for its own approach (short or long trades, a key spell to wait for…). Check the Matchups section to learn your champion’s strengths and weaknesses against each opponent.
LANING.CONTENT6: Baiting means getting your opponent to use an ability for nothing, so you can take advantage of the time it is on cooldown.

CONTENT7.LIST1: <bold>Fake an attack:</bold> step forward as if you were about to engage, then back off. If your opponent uses a spell to push you away or punish you, you can come back while it is on cooldown.
CONTENT7.LIST2: <bold>Stand at the edge:</bold> stay just within range of a poke or crowd-control spell, ready to dodge it. If they miss, they become vulnerable and you can counter-attack.
CONTENT7.LIST3: <bold>Use the minions:</bold> act like you are going for a low-health minion. Your opponent may be tempted to use a spell to punish you, which you can dodge.
CONTENT7.LIST4: <bold>Look weak:</bold> make it look like you are out of mana or health. Your opponent may then overextend, which lets you counter-attack or bring in your jungler.

LANING.CONTENT8: When an important enemy spell is on cooldown (an escape ability or a summoner spell like Flash, for example), that is the moment to engage or call your jungler.
LANING.CONTENT9:
Sometimes there is nothing left to do in your lane: your wave is crashing into the enemy tower and you do not have enough gold for a useful purchase. That is the time to go help elsewhere: roaming.

While your opponent farms under their tower, you can create a numbers advantage in another lane or around an objective.

Mid is the best lane for roaming, as it sits in the middle of the map, close to everything. Supports and top laners can also roam to help their allies or set up an objective.

A failed roam is costly: while you are away, you lose minions and experience. Only leave when your wave is pushed and the play has a good chance of working.

CONTENT10.LIST1: <bold>Help another lane:</bold> if your champion has good crowd control or mobility, a <term k="GANK">gank</term> on another lane can give your allies a decisive advantage.
CONTENT10.LIST2: <bold>Place vision:</bold> put down vision <term k="WARD">wards</term> in the enemy jungle or around your lane to see ganks coming.
CONTENT10.LIST3: <bold>Invade the enemy jungle:</bold> catch the enemy jungler in their jungle to deny their camps. Careful, their allies can come help: it is safer with your jungler or support.
CONTENT10.LIST4: <bold>Set up an objective:</bold> join your allies to take a dragon or another objective, placing vision around it before it spawns.

JUNGLE.SUBTITLE0: Master the game and give your team the decisive edge!

CONTENT1.INTRO1:
The jungler role is often considered the most impactful in a game of League of Legends.

The goal of a jungler is to make the best decisions to:
CONTENT1.LIST1: Help their team gain an advantage over direct opponents.
CONTENT1.LIST3: Accumulate 'free' resources by killing jungle monsters.
CONTENT1.LIST4: Anticipate ganks and movements of the enemy jungler.
CONTENT1.INTRO2: The main difficulty of the role, for beginners and experienced players alike: success depends less on your mechanical skill than on your ability to read the game and make the right calls at the right time.

CONTENT2.INTRO1: There are several possible paths (the order in which you <term k="CLEAR">clear</term> your camps). Pick yours from the loading screen, based on both teams’ champions:
CONTENT2.LIST1:
Full clear: all 6 camps of your jungle → Scuttle Crab → gank or back to base.
It is the most common path: it gives you the most gold and experience before your first gank, but you do not help your lanes during the first minutes.
CONTENT2.LIST2: <bold>3 camps → gank:</bold> Useful to apply early pressure and help a lane, or if your champion clears camps slowly. Careful: if the gank fails, you lose a lot of time and resources.
CONTENT2.LIST3:
1 camp + invade: Do your red or blue buff, then go straight into the enemy jungle on the same side of the map to steal their camp (that is what an invade is).
Only try it if you are sure the enemy jungler started on the other side (e.g. you start red and steal their blue while they start at their red). Also watch out for enemy laners coming to help.

CONTENT3.INTRO1: If you go for a full clear, the question is: finish on the bot side or the top side? It depends on several factors:
CONTENT3.LIST1: <bold>Read the lanes:</bold> some lanes naturally push more than others. For example, Tristana will push more easily against Ezreal, thanks to her area damage. Plan where you will finish your clear: if you want to gank bot, start top, and vice versa.
CONTENT3.LIST2: <bold>Read the summoner spells:</bold> if your top laner has Ignite and their opponent has Teleport, starting bot to finish with a top gank can be a good idea. Early on, a top laner without Teleport has a much harder time getting back to lane after dying.
CONTENT3.LIST3: <bold>Read the champions:</bold> some champions are strong early (like Pantheon), others shine late (like Veigar). Helping a late-game champion through their laning phase can win you the game in the long run. Either way, play around your team’s <term k="CARRY">carries</term>.

CONTENT4.INTRO1: Neutral objectives sit in two pits, on either side of the river:
CONTENT4.LIST1: <bold>Top side:</bold> Voidgrubs (8:00), then Rift Herald (15:00), then Baron Nashor (20:00).
CONTENT4.LIST2: <bold>Bot side:</bold> elemental drakes (from 5:00), then the Elder Dragon.

JUNGLE.CONTENT5:
Taking an objective usually requires outnumbering the enemy around it, which is why your laners’ priority matters. A lane has priority when its laner has pushed their wave: the opponent has to stay and farm under their tower, and your laner can reach the river first to help you.

Before starting an objective, tell your laners so they push their waves. A successful gank right before an objective spawns is also a good way to get that priority.

Avoid going back to base right before an objective spawns: if the enemy team sets up around it first, contesting it becomes much harder.

With priority, you can also punish the enemy jungler by invading their jungle, to steal camps or take them down.
JUNGLE.CONTENT6:
A gank is when a player, usually the jungler, shows up by surprise in a lane to attack the opponent with a numbers advantage.

Only gank when you have a good chance of success; otherwise, keep farming. A gank is successful if you get a kill or an assist, or force the opponent to use an important summoner spell like Flash. A failed gank wastes your time, and therefore gold and experience, and it is one of the biggest traps of the role.

The best targets: an opponent pushed up in their lane, far from their tower, often because your ally’s wave is pushed toward them.

Stay unseen: if the opponent sees you coming, the gank almost always fails. Avoid enemy wards, or disable them with the Oracle Lens.

CONTENT7.LIST1: <bold>Through the river:</bold> the most direct route, simple but effective. It is also the most watched: think about enemy vision.
CONTENT7.LIST2: <bold>Lane bush / counter-gank:</bold> wait hidden in a lane bush, either to surprise the opponent or to trap the enemy jungler as they come to gank your ally.
CONTENT7.LIST3: <bold>Dive:</bold> if the opponent is under their tower with low health and your ally’s wave is on the tower (to absorb its shots), you can attack them under their tower with your laner. Whoever goes in first takes the tower shots: plan who tanks them.

CONTENT8.LIST1: On your first back, swap your <term k="TRINKET">trinket</term> for the Oracle Lens: it disables enemy wards around you, which makes your ganks much harder to see coming.
CONTENT8.LIST2: With a champion who needs a lot of gold to be strong (Shyvana or Lillia, for example), gank less and focus on your farm.
CONTENT8.LIST3: Keep track of when you kill your camps: they respawn after a set delay. A well-timed path lets you find them ready when you come back.
CONTENT8.LIST4: Play around winning lanes. Spending too much time on a lane that is already lost can put the whole game at risk.
CONTENT8.LIST5: While you farm, keep an eye on the map and on where the waves are. Ping your team every time you spot the enemy jungler.
CONTENT8.LIST6: Talk to your allies with pings and chat: your objectives and ganks will be much better coordinated.

GAME.SUBTITLE0: Master the basics for a deeper understanding of the game!

CONTENT1.INTRO0:
Understanding stats is essential to pick your items.
Each stat changes how your champion behaves in a fight, and knowing how they work helps you buy the right items for the situation.

Here are the main stats in the game, what they do and who they are for.
CONTENT1.LIST1: <bold>Attack Damage (AD):</bold> increases the physical damage of your basic attacks and some abilities. Mostly used by marksmen, assassins and fighters.
CONTENT1.LIST2: <bold>Ability Power (AP):</bold> increases magic damage and the strength of many effects (heals, shields). Used by mages, many supports and some assassins.
CONTENT1.LIST3: <bold>Attack Speed (AS):</bold> the number of basic attacks per second. With 1.5 attack speed, your champion attacks 1.5 times per second.
CONTENT1.LIST4: <bold>Ability Haste (AH):</bold> reduces your abilities’ cooldowns. Each point lets you cast your spells about 1% more often: with 100 points, you cast them twice as often (cooldowns halved). The displayed cooldown reduction percentage grows more and more slowly, but every point keeps the same value.
CONTENT1.LIST5: <bold>Critical Strike Chance:</bold> the chance for a basic attack to be a critical strike. Since the 2026 season, a critical strike deals 200% of the attack’s damage for most champions, not counting items that increase critical damage (like Infinity Edge).
CONTENT1.LIST6: <bold>Movement Speed:</bold> how fast your champion moves.
CONTENT1.LIST7: <bold>Tenacity:</bold> reduces the duration of most <term k="CC">crowd control</term> (stuns, slows, roots…). It has no effect on airborne, suppression, stasis, nearsight and drowsy.
CONTENT1.LIST8: <bold>Health / Resource Regeneration:</bold> the health (or mana, energy) your champion recovers automatically over time.
CONTENT1.LIST9: <bold>Life Steal / Omnivamp:</bold> life steal heals you for a percentage of your basic attack damage; omnivamp for a percentage of all your damage, abilities included.
CONTENT1.LIST10: <bold>Armor / Magic Resist:</bold> reduce physical and magic damage taken, respectively. 100 armor halves physical damage, 200 divides it by three. The displayed reduction percentage grows more and more slowly, but every point keeps making you just as much tougher: about 1% more effective health. What matters is the balance with your health: resistances are worth more when you have a lot of health, and health is worth more when you have a lot of resistances.
CONTENT1.LIST11: <bold>Armor Penetration / Lethality:</bold> armor penetration ignores a percentage of the target’s armor, lethality ignores a flat amount (1 lethality = 1 armor ignored). Lethality is best against squishy targets with little armor: assassins favor it. The percentage is better against very tanky targets, like tanks: it is the usual choice for marksmen.
CONTENT1.LIST12: <bold>Magic Penetration:</bold> same principle as for armor, against magic resist: some flat, some percentage.

CONTENT2.LIST1: Your basic attacks slow the target.
CONTENT2.LIST2: They also burn the target: true damage over a few seconds.
CONTENT2.LIST4: The buff lasts 2 minutes. If you die with it, it goes to the champion who killed you.

CONTENT3.LIST2: Ability haste: your spells come back faster.
CONTENT3.LIST3: The buff lasts 2 minutes. If you die with it, it goes to the champion who killed you.

CONTENT4.LIST1: Spawns at 2:55 in each half of the river.
CONTENT4.LIST2: Killing it spawns a shrine that grants vision around it (without revealing camouflaged units) and speeds up allies who walk through it.

CONTENT5.TEXT:
The first drake spawns at 5:00, then a new one 5 minutes after the previous one dies. Each drake has an element drawn at random from those that have not appeared yet, and gives a permanent, stacking bonus to the whole team that kills it.

Once the 2nd drake is killed, the map transforms based on the 3rd one’s element: this is the Elemental Rift, and every following drake will be of that element.

The first team to kill 4 drakes gets the Dragon Soul of that element, a very strong bonus. The closer a team gets to soul, the more drakes resist it (Dragon Vengeance: up to 45% less damage taken from a team that already has 3). After the soul, only the Elder Dragon spawns.

GAME.CONTENT6:
Baron Nashor spawns at 20:00 in the top pit, and respawns 6 minutes after it dies.

Killing it gives every living member of the team the Hand of Baron for 3 minutes: bonus attack damage and ability power, a recall twice as fast, and an aura that empowers nearby minions. Those minions take much less damage and gain range: cannon minions can even hit a tower from outside its range.
GAME.CONTENT7:
The Rift Herald spawns only once per game, at 15:00, in the top pit. It despawns at 19:45 (19:55 if in combat) to make way for Baron Nashor at 20:00.

Killing it drops the Eye of the Herald, which must be picked up within 20 seconds. Using it summons the Herald and you ride it: you steer its charge, which builds up speed. If it slams into a tower, it deals massive damage to it, and it knocks up the enemy champions it hits.
GAME.CONTENT8:
Voidgrubs spawn only once, at 8:00: a group of 3 grubs in the top pit. They do not respawn, and despawn at 14:45 (14:55 if in combat), before the Herald arrives at 15:00.

Each grub killed gives the team a stack of “Touch of the Void”: your attacks and abilities deal extra damage over time to structures. With all 3 stacks, the team gets “Hunger of the Void”: when you attack a structure, allied Voidmites regularly spawn to attack it with you.

INFERNAL.NAME: Infernal Drake
INFERNAL.SOUL: Your attacks and abilities trigger an explosion that deals bonus damage (at most once every 3 seconds).
INFERNAL.TERRAIN: Burnt walls open up near the pit, blast cones appear, and embers you can pick up give a short speed boost and a little ability haste.

MOUNTAIN.NAME: Mountain Drake
MOUNTAIN.SOUL: After 5 seconds without taking damage, you gain a shield.
MOUNTAIN.TERRAIN: Rocks rise from the ground near the buffs, the raptors and the pit, and block some paths.

OCEAN.NAME: Ocean Drake
OCEAN.STACK: Restores 2% of your missing health every 5 seconds.
OCEAN.SOUL: Your damage heals you and restores mana over a few seconds (reduced against minions and monsters).
OCEAN.TERRAIN: Bushes grow larger, puddles appear and more healing fruits grow in the jungle.

CLOUD.NAME: Cloud Drake
CLOUD.STACK: +5% slow resistance and out-of-combat movement speed.
CLOUD.SOUL: +15% movement speed, greatly increased for a few seconds after using your ultimate.
CLOUD.TERRAIN: Air currents near the buffs, the raptors and the pit speed up anyone who walks through them.

HEXTECH.NAME: Hextech Drake
HEXTECH.SOUL: Your attacks and abilities trigger an electric arc that deals true damage, slows and bounces to nearby enemies (at most once every 8 seconds).
HEXTECH.TERRAIN: Hextech gates link some areas of the jungle, and the base, so you can travel between them instantly.

CHEMTECH.NAME: Chemtech Drake
CHEMTECH.STACK: +6% tenacity and heal and shield power.
CHEMTECH.SOUL: Below 50% health, you deal 13% more damage and take 13% less.
CHEMTECH.TERRAIN: Jungle plants mutate: healing fruits also grant a shield, and blast cones knock you twice as far.

ELDER.NAME: Elder Dragon
ELDER.SPAWN: 6 minutes after a team gets the Dragon Soul, then 6 minutes after each of its deaths. Since 2026, it is tougher than before.

MECANICS.SUBTITLE0: Get better and hit the opposing goals more effectively!
MECANICS.CEILINGSHOT_STEPS: Roll the ball towards a wall (without bouncing).;Follow the ball until it passes the round part of the wall.;Jump and boost at the moment of impact on the ball to reach the ceiling;Drift;Drop to keep the flip or jump from the ceiling;Hit the ball
MECANICS.CEILINGSHOT_EXPLICATION:
When the ball is high, it is often possible to use the ceiling to attack in a more unpredictable way than usual.
The ceiling shot allows you to be more comfortable with the ceiling, in addition to opening shooting angles that are not available with traditional aerial techniques, thus offering more diversity in offensive strategies.
MECANICS.FASTAERIAL_EXPLICATION:
The fast aerial allows you to reach the ball in the air faster than other players, which can be crucial for gaining an advantage during aerial duels.
Whether defending a shot or executing a quick attack, the fast aerial is a versatile technique that overall improves a player's performance.
MECANICS.WAVEDASH_STEPS: Slight jump;Air roll so the car is parallel to the ground;Lift the car upwards;Flip to land on the ground
MECANICS.WAVEDASH_EXPLICATION:
Wave dashes allow players to gain speed quickly while conserving boost. This can be crucial for reaching the ball faster or returning to defense.
Additionally, they allow for rapid and effective direction changes, which can surprise opponents and create play opportunities.

This technique can be used in various situations, whether on the ground or on walls, providing great flexibility in gameplay.
MECANICS.WALLTOAIRDRIBBLE_STEPS: Roll the ball towards a wall (without bouncing).;Follow the ball until it surpasses the round part of the wall.;Touch the ball and lift off just after that touch.;Aerial roll to straighten out.;Follow the ball in the air while managing your boost (aim for under the ball to keep it airborne as long as possible).;Aim for the opposing goals.
MECANICS.WALLTOAIRDRIBBLE_EXPLICATION:
This technique is a fundamental element of Rocket League, essential throughout your progression, regardless of your rank. It is particularly effective for surprising defenders, due to the multiple touches of the ball it involves.

However, avoid using it if an opponent is heading towards you before you reach the wall or if they are already on the wall. Additionally, if the ball bounces or is at supersonic speed (max speed), executing this technique will be more challenging.
MECANICS.HALFFLIP_STEPS: Jump;Backflip (Dash back: Joystick down + Jump);Cancel the backflip (Joystick up halfway through the flip animation to keep the car parallel to the ground);Air roll
MECANICS.HALFFLIP_EXPLICATION:
This is simply the best movement to return to defense (or attack) when your car is facing the wrong direction, while remaining dynamic on the field.
You will encounter a moment in every match where the half flip is crucial, such as during a bump, a poor challenge against an opponent, or repositioning after a bad decision, etc.
MECANICS.FLICK_DIAGONALBACKFLIP_STEPS: Jump;Turn horizontally to the right and vertically slightly upward;Left air roll;Diagonal back-left flick
MECANICS.FLICK_DIAGONALBACKFLIP_EXPLICATION:
This flick surprises your opponent due to its quick execution and keeps you well-positioned to return to defense efficiently.

Generally, it is advantageous to trigger it when you are at midfield; with some practice, this will be the perfect distance for the ball to be on target while remaining in a zone that allows for both defensive plays and aggressive follow-ups.

Technically, your main goal will be to initiate this flick with the ball in front of your car.
Simply turn your car slightly in one direction, combined with an air roll, and flick in the opposite direction (if you turn your car to the right of the ball, the flick will be triggered to the back left with the joystick: the ball will then go high to the left).

As you can see, in addition to quick execution, the directional change (unlike a front flick, for example) enhances the surprise effect of your offensive play (e.g., I dribble towards the opponent's goal on the right post side, I trigger this flick to the right of the ball, and the ball suddenly goes to the opponent's top corner left).
MECANICS.PINCH_KUXIR_STEPS: Roll the ball on the ground towards a wall, from the middle of your side;Jump towards the ball to impact it as it rolls on the wall (and not into the round part of the wall);Hit the ball slightly from the side opposite to the opposing goal;Flip into the wall at the moment of impact between the ball and the car.
MECANICS.PINCH_KUXIR_EXPLICATION:
Like many mechanics, this one can have a surprising effect, transforming a defense into a counter-attack or even a goal almost instantly. If you manage to master this pinch at least a bit, you can make a clearance that allows you to reposition yourself.

This pinch should not be attempted if your opponent is close to you or as close to the ball as you are; they can anticipate and counter you, which can play against you since you are in your half. Ideally, your opponent should also not be already positioned in defense in their goal: 90% of the time, you will just return the ball to them.

The best scenario is when you manage to accelerate the ball to one side while your opponent is taking the boost from the opposite side or is behind you.
MECANICS.MUSTYFLICK_STEPS: Jump after the bounce to send the ball up while following it (like an Air Dribble);Turn the car backward, boosting if necessary to avoid touching the ball;Perform a backflip
MECANICS.MUSTYFLICK_EXPLICATION:
The Musty Flick is an advanced mechanic that allows you to propel the ball with speed and an angle that is difficult for your opponent to anticipate. What makes this move particularly fearsome is the element of surprise it generates: when your car flips backward, the opponent generally expects you to land with the ball. However, triggering the flick at this precise moment catches your opponent off guard by sending the ball sharply upward.

This mechanic is not limited to simple execution; if you master 'Cancel Flips,' you can slightly delay the flick timing, giving you even more control and increasing your shot's power. This makes the action even more unpredictable and difficult to counter, adding an extra dimension to your offensive play.

HOME.SUBBIENVENUE: The ultimate hub for competitive gamers who want to improve
HOME.CONTENT1:
In the gaming world, the ascent to the top can often seem like an obstacle-filled journey, especially for beginner players. Generally, 85% of players are ranked Diamond or below, which is why I came up with the idea of creating a platform dedicated to those who aspire to improve their skills and progress in their game.

My goal with TeamUpp is simple: to gather, in one place, all the information you need to progress in your favorite games. No more struggling to find answers to your questions or navigating through different sources. Here, you will find structured guides, clear tips, and strategies directly accessible for several competitive games.

I want to make learning simple, effective, and above all accessible to everyone.
HOME.CONTENT2: Instead of spending hours digging through forums or browsing scattered videos on YouTube, TeamUpp gathers everything a beginner player needs in one place. Whether you are new or just want to refine your skills, we provide you with practical guides, tips, and strategies, carefully organized for smooth and intuitive navigation.
HOME.CONTENT3: We believe that every player deserves a chance to shine. That’s why we are committed to making learning accessible and engaging. Our content is designed to be easily understandable, even for those who have never touched a competitive game before.
HOME.CONTENT4: In addition to our resources, TeamUpp aims to be a true community. We encourage interaction among players, allowing everyone to share experiences, exchange tips, and support each other in their quest for progress. Together, we build an environment where everyone can thrive and feel supported.

HOME.CONTENT5:
Join us today and discover how TeamUpp can transform your gaming experience. Together, let’s make your gaming journey a rewarding and successful adventure.

Your ascent begins here!

TFT.CONTENT1:
TFT is an “auto-battler” strategy game: you recruit a team of champions from the League of Legends universe, place them on a board, and they automatically fight the other players’ teams.

Each game brings together eight players, who start with 100 health. When you lose a fight, you lose health: a fixed amount that grows with each stage, plus 1 per enemy unit still alive.
At 0 health, you are eliminated. Your placement depends on the order of elimination: the last player standing finishes 1st, and finishing in the top 4 counts as a win.

The game is split into stages, themselves split into rounds (2-1, 2-2…). After a first stage against monsters, every stage follows the same pattern:

LIST1.CONTENT0: <bold>3 PvP fights:</bold> three fights against other players, drawn at random while avoiding those you just faced.
LIST1.CONTENT1: <bold>Carousel:</bold> each player in turn picks a champion holding an item component. Players with the least health pick first.
LIST1.CONTENT2: <bold>2 PvP fights:</bold> two more fights against other players.
LIST1.CONTENT3: <bold>PvE round:</bold> the stage ends against monsters, which drop gold, components or champions.
LIST1.OUTRO:
The goal: build the best team you can to beat the other players and survive as long as possible.

At rounds 2-1, 3-2 and 4-2, you also pick an augment out of three options: a permanent bonus that can shape your whole game.
LIST1.OUTRO1: In the player list, an icon appears next to the opponents you have not faced yet during the current stage: they are your possible next opponents. Check their boards to adapt your positioning.

TFT.CONTENT2: TFT is built on four core concepts:
TFT.CONTENT3:
In the current set, there are five champion rarities.
The rarer a champion, the more expensive and powerful it is, and the fewer copies there are in the shared pool:

LIST3.OUTRO0:
Upgrading your champions is key to getting the most out of them.

Every champion is 1 star when you buy it. With three copies of the same 1-star champion, they automatically combine into a 2-star champion, much stronger: more health, more damage, and often a stronger spell. Same principle afterwards: three 2-star copies make a 3-star champion, its most powerful version.
Rarity matters a lot: the rarer a champion, the higher its base stats, so upgrading a rare champion (Tier 4, for example) has far more impact than upgrading a common one (Tier 1).
LIST3.OUTRO1: Understanding upgrades is not enough: you also need to watch <bold>your opponents’ teams</bold>. All eight players draw from the same <bold>champion pool</bold>, which holds a <bold>limited number of copies</bold> of each champion. Every copy an opponent buys is one less for you: if several players want the same champion, upgrading it becomes very hard.
LIST3.OUTRO2: The key: <bold>watch your opponents’ compositions</bold> to aim for less contested champions, which you will have a better chance of upgrading. Good <bold>economy management</bold> and <bold>careful scouting of the other players</bold> will keep your progress from stalling.

TFT.CONTENT4:
Components are mini-items. Combining two components on a champion creates a full item. Each champion can hold up to three items. Depending on the set, there are also special items: radiant items (upgraded versions), artifacts, or emblems, crafted with a Spatula, which give an extra trait to the champion holding them.

Each champion has a role (tank, physical damage, magic damage…), shown in game to help you equip it. Items fall into broad families, such as damage items and defensive items.
Put your items on the most important champions of your team, your carries, while respecting their role: a defensive item on a tank, a damage item on an attacker. This logic is the foundation of an effective team.

Also look at your opponents’ items: it helps you anticipate their strategies and pick items that counter them.
TFT.CONTENT6: Managing your gold well lets you control your game. Every round, you receive a base income of 5 gold (a bit less during the very first rounds). On top of that come <bold>interest</bold>: bonus gold based on the gold you keep in reserve.

LIST6.CONTENT0: 1 gold of interest per 10 gold, up to 5 gold from 50 gold. Beyond 50 gold, saving more does not earn anything extra.
LIST6.CONTENT1: Winning a fight against a player earns 1 extra gold, which often helps reach the next threshold.

TFT.CONTENT7: Win or loss streaks also earn bonus gold (a 2-round streak earns nothing):

LIST7.CONTENT0: <bold>3 or 4 wins or losses in a row:</bold> +1 gold.
LIST7.CONTENT1: <bold>5 wins or losses in a row:</bold> +2 gold.
LIST7.CONTENT2: <bold>6 or more wins or losses in a row:</bold> +3 gold.

TFT.CONTENT8:
Your level matters just as much. You gain 2 XP for free every round, and you can buy experience: 4 gold for 4 XP. Your level (10 at most) sets how many champions you can field on the board: at level 5, you can field 5. It also changes the odds of each rarity in the shop: the higher your level, the more rare champions you see.

There are different economy strategies. Some players prefer to save and accept a few losses to come back with a lot of gold, others, like me, choose an aggressive approach to keep as much health as possible. Keep in mind that 80 gold in your pocket is useless if you are eliminated.

Beginners are often afraid to spend their gold. My advice: watch your health bar first, it is what matters most. If your team is too weak, do not hesitate to spend.

Make thoughtful decisions. When to buy XP? When to refresh the shop (called “rolling”)? There is no perfect moment: it all depends on your game and your health.
Ask yourself every round: is buying XP worth it? Yes or no? Why? Is refreshing the shop worth it with my level and my health? With experience, the answers will come naturally.

LIST9.CONTENT0: <bold>Do not blame luck:</bold> the shop has some randomness, but over several games your decisions make the difference. After a bad game, look for what you could have done differently.
LIST9.CONTENT1:
Step back every round: analyze the situation to make the most logical choice.
Why buy XP? Why refresh the shop? Why do nothing?
LIST9.CONTENT2: <bold>Watch and learn:</bold> in TFT, watching good players (on YouTube or on stream) teaches a lot, sometimes more than playing yourself. Build up knowledge, then apply it in your games.
LIST9.CONTENT3: <bold>Top 4 = win:</bold> do not aim for 1st place every game. Finishing top 4 is a win: consistency is the key.
LIST9.CONTENT4: <bold>Be flexible:</bold> do not lock yourself into a single composition or champion. If you are above an interest threshold, buy champions even if they do not fit your composition: a 1-star champion sells back for its full price, so it costs you nothing, and it can let you switch compositions much more easily. A very good player sees transitions a beginner does not: that is how you improve your team efficiently.
LIST9.CONTENT5: <bold>Influence the shop:</bold> since all players draw from the same pool, buying other champions of the same cost as the one you are looking for very slightly increases your chances of finding it.

GLOSSARY.WAVE: Wave: the group of minions that leaves each base at regular intervals and walks down each lane.
GLOSSARY.GANK: Gank: a surprise attack by a player coming from elsewhere (usually the jungler) on a lane, to outnumber the opponent.
GLOSSARY.CRASH: Crash: when your minion wave reaches the enemy tower and gets destroyed by it.
GLOSSARY.BACK: Back: going back to base (Recall, B key) to buy items and restore health and mana.
GLOSSARY.SLOW_PUSH: Slow push: moving the wave forward slowly so it grows before reaching the enemy tower.
GLOSSARY.LAST_HIT: Last hit: the killing blow on a minion or monster. It is what earns the gold.
GLOSSARY.ROAM: Roam: leaving your lane for a moment to help elsewhere on the map.
GLOSSARY.DIVE: Dive: attacking an opponent under their own tower, accepting to take the tower’s shots.
GLOSSARY.PRIO: Priority (prio): your laner has pushed their wave, so the opponent has to stay and farm it under their tower. Your laner can therefore leave the lane first.
GLOSSARY.ADC: ADC (Attack Damage Carry): the team’s marksman, a ranged champion who deals most of their damage with basic attacks.
GLOSSARY.TRADE: Trade: an exchange of damage between two opponents. The goal: deal more than you take.
GLOSSARY.COOLDOWN: Cooldown: a spell’s recharge time, during which it cannot be used.
GLOSSARY.BAIT: Bait: luring the opponent into wasting a spell.
GLOSSARY.POKE: Poke: harassing the opponent from range with attacks or abilities, without committing to a real fight.
GLOSSARY.SPACING: Spacing: managing the distance between you and your opponent, so you can hit them without being hit.
GLOSSARY.POWERSPIKE: Power spike: a moment when a champion suddenly gets much stronger (level 6 and their ultimate, a finished item…).
GLOSSARY.WARD: Ward: an object placed on the ground that grants vision of the area around it, to see enemies coming.
GLOSSARY.TRINKET: Trinket: the free utility item slot (key 4). It holds your choice of Stealth Ward (yellow, places an invisible ward), Oracle Lens (red, disables nearby enemy wards) or, from level 9, Farsight Alteration (blue, reveals an area from afar).
GLOSSARY.CC: Crowd control (CC): any effect that hinders a champion: stun, slow, root, knock-up…
GLOSSARY.CLEAR: Clear: killing every monster in a camp, or every camp on a path.
GLOSSARY.INVADE: Invade: entering the enemy jungle to steal their camps or catch the enemy jungler.
GLOSSARY.CARRY: Carry: the champion who “carries” the team, dealing most of the damage and deciding the fights.
GLOSSARY.AUGMENT: Augment: a permanent bonus picked from three options at set rounds. It can boost your economy, your items or your traits.
